`r tb <- \(f) read.csv(file.path("../../03.outputs/tables", f), check.names = FALSE); ev <- \(what, col = "value", m = "local") { t <- tb("T5_evaluation.csv"); t[[col]][t$model == m & t$metric == what] }; smp <- \(what) { t <- tb("T2_sample.csv"); t$n[t$step == what] }; fmt <- \(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","); acc <- \(cls) if (cls == "nest") 100 * ev("Nest cells above threshold") / ev("Nest cells") else 100 * (1 - ev("Background cells above threshold") / ev("Background cells")); trimws(format(as.Date("2026-11-22"), "%e %B %Y"))`

The Editors\
*Forest Ecology and Management*

Dear Editors,

I submit the research paper "`r rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter("../Manuscript-20261122.qmd")$title`" for consideration in *Forest Ecology and Management*.

The Marbled Murrelet, a seabird listed as threatened in Canada and the United States, nests in old-growth coniferous forest. In British Columbia, the forest retained for it is chosen with habitat models. Cosgrove et al. (2024) built such a model from airborne laser scans and located nests in Desolation Sound, where it reached an area under the curve (AUC) of `r fmt(ev("AUC", m = "desolation"))`. Transferred to Clayoquot Sound, it reached `r fmt(ev("AUC", m = "transferred"))`. The paper tested whether the same model, rebuilt from Clayoquot Sound's own radio-tracked nests and the province's public 2019 laser scans, would do better.

The local model, rebuilt from `r smp("nest cells in available forest")` nest cells and `r fmt(smp("background cells in available forest"), 0)` background cells in tall forest unharvested since 1998 and scored on spatially separate folds, could not be distinguished from chance. The model classed `r fmt(acc("nest"), 1)` percent of held-out nest cells and `r fmt(acc("background"), 1)` percent of background cells correctly, an average accuracy of `r fmt((acc("nest") + acc("background")) / 2, 1)` percent. The model's AUC of `r fmt(ev("AUC"))` (95 percent confidence interval `r fmt(ev("AUC", "low"))` to `r fmt(ev("AUC", "high"))`) included both chance and the `r fmt(ev("AUC", m = "transferred"))` of the transferred model. Nest cells had more internal forest gaps than background cells, though not significantly. The result held when the cells were enlarged to 4 and 9 ha, across 20 other fold assignments, and in three further refits of the model.

For forest managers, a model fitted to the few located nests in Clayoquot Sound gave no reason to replace the transferred model. The paper names two tests that public data already allow, a model fitted to nests pooled across regions and measures of individual tall trees taken from the scans.

Every line of code that built, fitted and scored the model is held in the public manuscript source. The nest locations, laser scans and harvest records are all public.

The manuscript has not been published and is not under consideration by another journal. I am its sole author and declare no competing interests.

Yours sincerely,

Seamus Murphy, MSc, PhD
